title: An Analyst's Guide to MMM | Robyn

facts.fact: MMM is described by the guide as a privacy-friendly, highly resilient, data-driven statistical analysis that quantifies the incremental sales impact and ROI of marketing and non-marketing activities.
facts.quote: Marketing mix modeling (MMM) is a privacy-friendly, highly resilient, data-driven statistical analysis that quantifies the incremental sales impact and ROI of marketing and non-marketing activities.

facts.fact: The guide gives an approximate timing of 1-2 weeks for the 'Define business questions and scope' step of an MMM study, for a first study.
facts.quote: note that these are typical timings for when you run the first study and that this can be shortened for refresh models

facts.fact: The guide gives an approximate timing of 4-6 weeks for the data collection step of an MMM study.
facts.quote: Data collection is one of the most important but time consuming steps in an MMM study.

facts.fact: The guide gives an approximate timing of 1-2 weeks for the data review step of an MMM study.
facts.quote: In addition to data collection, data review is one of the most important steps in an MMM study.

facts.fact: The guide gives an approximate timing of 4-8 weeks for the modeling step of an MMM study, depending on MMM scope.
The guide gives an approximate timing of 2-4 weeks for the analysis and recommendations step of an MMM study.
facts.quote: Analysis and recommendations | Once happy with the model, the next step is to analyse the data outputs

facts.fact: The guide states that the approximate step timings are typical for a first study and can be shortened for refresh models and/or for the method of implementation (in-house vs. partner).
facts.quote: this can be shortened for refresh models and/or the method of implementation (e.g. in-house vs. partner)

facts.fact: The guide states there are three widely accepted methods to implement an MMM (DIY, SaaS, and 3rd party vendors).
facts.quote: There are three widely accepted methods to implement a MMM.

facts.fact: The guide says that working with a 3rd party MMM vendor can allow comparison of MMM results with benchmarks, depending on the vendor.
facts.quote: can compare your MMM results with benchmarks (depending on the vendor)

facts.fact: The guide says that 3rd party MMM vendors charge a fee and are usually the most expensive of the MMM implementation options.
facts.quote: Vendor will charge a fee, usually the most expensive option when compared to other options.
